cards.title: Endpoint-specific noncompartmental eligibility and sparse-design scope
cards.claim: Decide separately which NCA endpoints are supported: observed Cmax/Tmax, finite-window AUC, and single-dose terminal-dependent AUCinf/half-life/CL/Vz/moments. Distinguish individual serial profiles from destructive-sampling mean profiles. A blocked tail need not block descriptive or finite-window quantities.
conditions: Choose the explicitly qualified branch; scientific scope and assumptions are specified in method_recipe.
required_inputs: Use the branch-specific input contract below; unknown inputs remain unknown.
limitations: Offline candidate pending source and operational review; no target-human facts, fitting or production use.
cards.downstream_use: Plan an evidence-bounded method and identify blocked dependent outputs; ContextBuilder supplies project objective separately.

method_recipe.estimand_and_scope: Decide separately which NCA endpoints are supported: observed Cmax/Tmax, finite-window AUC, and single-dose terminal-dependent AUCinf/half-life/CL/Vz/moments. Distinguish individual serial profiles from destructive-sampling mean profiles. A blocked tail need not block descriptive or finite-window quantities.
method_recipe.input_contract: Require time/unit and dosing reference; concentration/unit, matrix/analyte/basis, censor flag and bound; route/dose; design-unit IDs or explicitly unknown status; integration rule/window. Sparse summaries additionally require time-specific n and design/correlation information for uncertainty. Terminal outputs require justified phase selection, model and extrapolation assumptions.
method_recipe.applicability_and_prerequisites: Establish comparable sampling/design and valid integration domain. Phoenix sparse calculations use mean concentrations at each time; its equal-n/no-missing restrictions apply to that documented implementation, especially batch repeated-subject designs. Unequal independent destructive sample sizes do not alone prove every mean-curve estimator biased. Qualify the actual estimator.
method_recipe.definitions_units_basis_window: Observed Cmax has concentration units, Tmax time, AUC concentration*time and lambda_z 1/time. Label observed maximum rather than unknown true continuous-time maximum. Preserve BLQ as a censor event with its bound; do not silently convert it to zero or an exact imputed concentration. This preservation is a reviewer guardrail: SUP001 reports bias for tested model-estimation substitution/omission methods, not a universally proven NCA integration policy.
method_recipe.procedure: Produce an endpoint eligibility table with reason for every blocked quantity. For finite AUC state exact start/end, time handling and chosen integration rule; do not invent unobserved endpoints. Examine a plausible terminal log-linear region separately; a numerical minimum point count or R2 alone cannot establish it. For sparse designs label mean-curve results and use design-appropriate uncertainty only.
method_recipe.formula_and_parameterization: Linear-trapezoid finite AUC=sum_i [((C_i+C_(i+1))/2)*(t_(i+1)-t_i)], a mathematical expansion of the source method. If a valid terminal approximation exists, AUCinf=AUC0t+Ct/lambda_z; the source-defined last observed/predicted Ct choice must be recorded. No terminal approximation means no AUCinf. Dependent CL and moments follow their own route-qualified definitions, not Dose/AUClast.
method_recipe.uncertainty_and_identifiability: Separate sampling variability, tail-model uncertainty and individual variability. A mean profile does not recover individual trajectories/parameter distributions. Sparse uncertainty must respect covariance from repeated animals; source-specific variance assumptions are not universally applicable. Do not attach confidence intervals if the required design/variance information is absent.
method_recipe.diagnostics_and_failure_modes: Late BLQ may constrain a tail but does not automatically invalidate every possible qualified earlier slope. Rising or mixed distribution/absorption segments cannot simply be labeled terminal elimination. Preserve censored and missing observations distinctly. No universal three-point/R2 scientific pass criterion is used.
method_recipe.missing_input_and_partial_fallback: Without a qualified tail, retain supported finite AUC and observed descriptors with explicit window/basis. If censoring makes numerical integration ambiguous, report the unresolved handling or a justified bound rather than choose zero/LLOQ2. Missing individual IDs prohibits invented serial curves but can permit qualified aggregate descriptions. The separately qualified steady-state IV CLss=Dose_per_interval/AUC_tau branch is covered by G02 and need not estimate a terminal slope when interval AUC is supported.
method_recipe.output_and_interpretation: Report endpoint, value/unit if eligible, integration/design choices, censor handling, source provenance and limitations. Mean-profile CL or volume is explicitly a derived mean-profile quantity, not a mean or distribution of individual CL/volume.
method_recipe.worked_example_and_counterexample: SYNTHETIC finite-window fixture: exact observed C=[0,2,4] mg/L at t=[0,1,2] h yields linear AUC0-2=1+3=4 mg*h/L, observed Cmax=4 mg/L at 2 h. Rising data establish no terminal slope, AUCinf or CL; Dose/AUC0-2 must not be labeled clearance. Counterexample: if the first value is BLQ rather than exact zero, this numerical AUC is not automatically permitted.

claim_support.claim: NCA parameters are categorized into those requiring Lambda Z estimation (terminal-dependent) and those that do not (finite-window/descriptive).
claim_support.scope: Source-defined single-dose parameters: AUClast/Cmax versus extrapolated AUCinf and its dependent quantities. Not a claim that every steady-state CL estimate needs lambda_z.

claim_support.claim: Sparse sampling NCA calculates parameters from a mean concentration curve derived from unique time points, not individual serial profiles.
claim_support.scope: Phoenix NCA object treats sparse data by calculating mean concentration for each unique time value.

claim_support.claim: Bailer finite AUC0t in SUP005 uses linear trapezoids. Finite-window AUC does not itself require a terminal extrapolation, but its selected integration rule must be stated.
claim_support.scope: Source-specific linear-trapezoid method and qualified finite-window interpretation; other NCA integration choices are not excluded.
